PullRequest.Title: Add Copilot agent file schema support
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Adds table-driven Copilot `*.agent.md` schema support on top of #342855.

- Defines typed metadata for all Copilot custom-agent attributes, accepted YAML shapes, required fields, enums, defaults, and array item types.
- Uses the schema for property completions, finite value completions, hovers, supported-name checks, and generic validation.
- Adds semantic validation for models, model policy, legacy `infer`, GitHub MCP configuration, and local/remote agent-scoped MCP servers.
- Adds the current Copilot agent hook model: 15 canonical events, compatibility aliases, command/HTTP/startup-prompt actions, event-specific validation, type-aware completions, and hovers.
- Keeps Copilot agent hook metadata separate from VS Code's executable `HookType`/extension API union.
- Adds static nested completion support for GitHub and MCP properties while leaving live model/tool/skill inventories to #342881.
- Marks unsupported Local-only attributes unused for Copilot while retaining useful hover guidance.

This PR is stacked on #342855 and is part of #342854.

## Testing

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- Targeted ESLint for changed schema, language-provider, and test files — passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptHeaderAutocompletion.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptValidator.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptHovers.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptCodeActions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/hookSchema.test.ts` — passed, 333 tests

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or edit a GitHub Copilot *.agent.md file and receive diagnostics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The visible model is parsed, then validation runs after the existing 200 ms ModelTracker debounce; the new schema, hook, GitHub, and MCP checks are synchronous in-memory scans before markers are published. Existing body file-reference checks remain awaited on the diagnostics critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check existence of each same-scheme body file reference
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing fileService.exists call per body file reference, coalesced only by the 200 ms document validation debounce and run concurrently with Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-reference filesystem checks ran before this PR; the added header-schema validation does not add references or change their scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All checks are awaited before updated diagnostics are published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether a migrated agent file can be created for a legacy .chatmode.md file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call per validation of a legacy agent file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before diagnostics complete for that legacy-file scenario.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Header attributes, hook events/actions and MCP servers/properties; each new validator walk is linear in those parsed collections. Typical schemas contain tens of entries, and edits are coalesced by the existing per-model delayer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One delayed validation task per visible text model. Existing file-reference existence checks within one document fan out through Promise.all; the diff neither adds calls nor changes this concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed AST is cached by model URI and version, so validation reuses it within a version and reparses once after a content change. Static schema metadata is module-scoped; validation constructs only bounded temporary arrays, maps, and sets.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration, debounce, AST caching, new loops, and all transitive filesystem calls were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large hand-authored hook or MCP maps increase linear CPU and short-lived allocation, but realistic files are small and validation is debounced; no evidence supports user-visible latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded linear in-memory validation and does not introduce or amplify an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request header, nested GitHub/MCP, or hook completions while editing an agent file
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The completion provider retrieves the version-cached AST, locates the containing attribute/server/action, builds a small completion list, and returns it synchronously except for pre-existing model/agent inventory paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Top-level attributes are bounded by the static schema; nested MCP completion location scales linearly with configured servers and properties, while hook completion location scales linearly with hook events/actions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single provider invocation performs one local scan; there is no added queue, fan-out, IPC, filesystem, subprocess, database, or network operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm requests on an unchanged model reuse the cached AST. A changed model incurs one parse that is then cached by version. Static schema tables are reused, while small completion arrays and sets are rebuilt per request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the completion entry point and all new nested helper paths were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Completion can be invoked frequently during typing, but the added work is bounded or linear over realistically small frontmatter collections and has no expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added scans and allocations are small, request-local, and proportional to the frontmatter being completed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover over Copilot agent attributes, hook events, or hook action properties
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The hover provider reads the version-cached AST, scans header attributes and hook properties until the hovered range is found, then creates one MarkdownString.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of header attributes and hook-event properties in the current file; metadata lookup is constant-time after the range scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous local lookup per hover request with no asynchronous boundary or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The AST is reused for the current model version; module-scoped schema and hook metadata are reused across hovers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the provider and changed metadata lookup path were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hover frequency varies, but the diff adds only constant-time metadata lookup after existing linear containment scans.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The richer metadata does not trigger heavier rendering, I/O, or retained state.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 10 changed files and every diff page. The PR adds static schema metadata plus bounded linear validation/completion/hover work. Parsing remains version-cached, diagnostics remain debounced, and no subprocess, IPC, network, database, or new filesystem work is introduced. No valid performance finding or evidenced shipped-regression fix was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
